jsondiff.identicalNote: Both documents hold the same structure and values (key order aside).
jsondiff.idle: Fill both sides with valid JSON to see the differences
jsondiff.allFiltered: Nothing to show under the current filter
jsondiff.dropHint: Drop a .json on either pane; drop two at once to fill both
jsondiff.truncated: Too many differences; showing the first 2000
jsondiff.filterHint: A kind you turn off is left out of the copied report too
jsondiff.aboutKeys: Objects compare by key, and key order is never a difference — which is exactly what a text diff cannot do.
jsondiff.aboutArrays: Arrays compare in order, but anchor on the items that did not move, so inserting at the front does not repaint the whole array.
jsondiff.aboutPaths: Paths use the same spelling as the JSONPath box in JSON Format, so they paste straight across.
jsondiff.scopeHint: A query starting with $ keeps that subtree and nothing beside it; anything else is matched as a fragment of the path. The crosshair on a row scopes to it.

idgen.kindUuid4: Purely random, 122 bits of entropy. Universal, but as a primary key it scatters index writes across the whole tree.
idgen.kindUuid7: The first 48 bits are a millisecond timestamp, so string order is time order — the one to reach for as a key.
idgen.kindUlid: 26 Crockford base32 characters, time-sortable, and free of I/L/O/U so it survives being read aloud.
idgen.kindNano: URL-safe and shorter than a UUID at comparable collision odds.
idgen.formatHint: UUIDs only: ULID is defined in upper case and Nano ID's alphabet is case-sensitive, so folding either changes what it is.
idgen.aboutSource: Randomness comes from crypto.getRandomValues, never Math.random — these end up in databases and URLs, and a predictable id is a problem in both.
idgen.aboutSort: Everything is generated locally; nothing is fetched.

fake.aboutChecksum: ID numbers carry an ISO 7064 MOD 11-2 check character and card numbers a Luhn digit — data the form under test rejects has exercised nothing.
fake.aboutPrivacy: Only the region prefixes come from a published table; every other digit is random, so a generated number belongs to nobody.
fake.aboutCopy: Click a cell to copy it; the buttons above copy the whole table as TSV, CSV or JSON.

color.bad: Not a colour this can read
color.idle: Enter a colour to see it in every format
color.largeHint: Large means 18pt, or 14pt bold, where the bar is 3:1 / 4.5:1 instead of 4.5:1 / 7:1. Heavier strokes hold up at lower contrast; applying this to body text only fools you.

unit.idle: Enter an amount to see every unit
unit.noteExact: Factors are the defined ones: an inch is exactly 0.0254 m and a pound exactly 0.45359237 kg, by definition rather than approximation.
unit.noteData: Decimal and binary prefixes are different things: 1 kB is 1000 B, 1 KiB is 1024 B. That gap is why a drive looks smaller than the box said.
unit.noteTemp: Temperature carries an offset as well as a factor, so °F to K has to go through °C — a ratio-only table gets it wrong.
unit.noteYear: A year here is the Julian year of 365.25 days, which is what it means in any exact context.
unit.noteGallon: US and UK gallons differ by about 20%; both are listed.

imgdiff.pickHint: Drop or choose two images; the first two become A and B
imgdiff.sizeWarn: The two images differ in size: they are aligned top-left at the larger size, so the extra area counts as changed.
imgdiff.thHint: JPEG carries compression noise, and a threshold of 0 lights up the whole frame. The default 2% drops the noise without hiding real edits.
imgdiff.overlayHint: "Mark changes" fades image B in underneath, so you can see where on the picture the changes are.

http.searchHint: The notes are searched too — typing "not allowed" finds 403.
http.tip401: 401 means no credentials or bad ones; 403 means valid credentials without permission. The name Unauthorized actually describes unauthenticated.
http.tip307: 301/302 were historically rewritten from POST to GET by clients; 307/308 explicitly keep the method and body.
http.tip422: 400 is a malformed request; 422 is a well-formed one whose content fails validation.
http.s100: Go ahead and send the body
http.s101: Switching protocols, e.g. upgrading to WebSocket
http.s301: Permanent redirect; old clients may turn POST into GET
http.s302: Temporary redirect; may also rewrite the method
http.s303: Fetch the other URL with GET, typically after a POST
http.s304: Not modified, use the cache; carries no body
http.s307: Temporary redirect keeping method and body
http.s308: Permanent redirect keeping method and body
http.s400: The request itself is wrong, e.g. malformed
http.s401: Unauthenticated: no credentials, or invalid ones
http.s404: Not found; also used to avoid revealing whether it exists
http.s405: Method not supported here; the response must carry Allow
http.s409: Conflicts with the current state, e.g. concurrent edits
http.s428: Send a precondition so you do not overwrite someone else
http.s501: The server does not implement the method
http.s503: Temporarily unavailable, e.g. overload or maintenance
http.hAccept: Media types the client will take
http.hContentDisposition: inline or attachment, and the download filename
http.hContentType: Media type of the body, with charset
http.hETag: Version of the resource, paired with If-None-Match
http.hIfNoneMatch: Send the ETag you have; 304 if unchanged
http.hLocation: Redirect target, or where the new resource lives
http.hRange: Ask for part of it, e.g. bytes=0-1023
http.hRetryAfter: How long to wait, in seconds or as a date
http.hSetCookie: Sets a cookie; mind SameSite and Secure
http.hVary: Which request headers the cache key depends on
http.hXff: Original client IP through a proxy; forgeable
http.hCors: Which origins may read the response; cannot be * with credentials

md.aboutLinks: Only http/https/mailto/tel and relative targets become links; javascript: and friends never do.
md.aboutSubset: Headings, emphasis, inline and fenced code, lists (nested, with task items), quotes, rules, tables, images and links.

lines.aboutRegex: The .* toggle switches a filter to regex. A half-typed pattern matches no lines rather than emptying the document.

csv.aboutQuotes: Parsed per RFC 4180 rather than split on the delimiter — one field with a comma in it shifts every later column, silently.
csv.aboutDetect: Delimiter detection counts candidates outside quotes; otherwise "Smith, John";42 looks comma-separated.

svg.aboutScripts: SVG is a document format and can carry
